description.en: Brief Mongol occupation of most of Syria in 1260 (Damascus taken; general Kitbuqa sent 'to occupy Damascus and reconnoiter in Palestine and trans-Jordan'). Raiding detachments reached Nablus and Gaza; ended by the Mamluk victory at Ayn Jalut, 3 Sept 1260.
description.ar: احتلال مغولي وجيز لمعظم سوريا عام 1260 (أُخذت دمشق؛ أُرسل القائد كتبغا 'to occupy Damascus and reconnoiter in Palestine and trans-Jordan' [لاحتلال دمشق واستطلاع فلسطين وشرق الأردن]). وصلت مفارز مغيرة إلى نابلس وغزة؛ وانتهى ذلك بانتصار المماليك في عين جالوت، 3 أيلول/سبتمبر 1260.
description.he: כיבוש מונגולי קצר של רוב סוריה ב-1260 (דמשק נלקחה; המצביא כיתבוקה נשלח “to occupy Damascus and reconnoiter in Palestine and trans-Jordan” [לכבוש את דמשק ולסייר בפלשתינה ובעבר הירדן]). יחידות פשיטה הגיעו לשכם/נאבלוס ולעזה; הדבר הסתיים בניצחון הממלוכים בעין ג׳אלות, 3 בספטמבר 1260.

sources.quote: the general Kitbuqa was dispatched to the south with a division to occupy Damascus and reconnoiter in Palestine and trans-Jordan.
defeating Kitbuqa on 3 September 1260 at ʿAyn Jālut in northern Palestine, thereby ending the short period of Mongol rule west of the Euphrates.
Twice the Mongols were successful in occupying most of Syria: in 658/1260 and 699/1299–1300. In both cases the Mongol conquest lasted for only a few months
the Mongol conquest of Palestine was never really completed, but was quite tenuous at best.
Finally, it is quite clear that the Mongols did enter, and terrorize, Jerusalem.
With Baalbek and Nablus taken, the Mongol occupation of Lebanon and Palestine was effectively completed (although, oddly enough, they seem never to have entered Jerusalem)
has stated that the Mongol detachments never reached Jerusalem itself.

notes.en: Scholars differ on the depth of control: Humphreys (1977) saw the occupation of Palestine as 'effectively completed' but thought the Mongols never entered Jerusalem and did not hold Transjordan; Runciman (1954) also held that they never reached Jerusalem; Amitai (1987) argues the conquest of Palestine was 'tenuous at best', but that Mongols did enter Jerusalem and conquered most of Transjordan. All partial units = raids/tenuous control, not administration.

description.en: After the Mongol victory at Wadi al-Khaznadar near Homs (end of 1299) Ghazan's forces occupied Damascus for about 100 days (the citadel held out); a raiding force under Mulay reached Gaza and committed abuses in Jerusalem and Hebron before withdrawing in early 1300.
description.ar: بعد الانتصار المغولي في وادي الخزندار قرب حمص (نهاية 1299) احتلت قوات غازان دمشق نحو 100 يوم (صمدت القلعة)؛ ووصلت قوة مغيرة بقيادة مولاي إلى غزة وارتكبت تجاوزات في القدس والخليل قبل انسحابها في أوائل 1300.
description.he: לאחר הניצחון המונגולי בוואדי אל-ח׳זנדאר ליד חומס (סוף 1299) כבשו כוחותיו של ע׳אזאן את דמשק לכ-100 יום (המצודה החזיקה מעמד); כוח פשיטה בפיקודו של מולאי הגיע לעזה ביצע מעשי התעללות בירושלים ובחברון לפני שנסוג בתחילת 1300.

sources.quote: An invasion of Syria at the end of 1299 led to the Mongol victory at the Wādi al-Ḵaznadār near Homs
The victory led to a 100-day Mongol occupation of Damascus, but the Mongols withdrew of their own accord
Twice the Mongols were successful in occupying most of Syria: in 658/1260 and 699/1299–1300. In both cases the Mongol conquest lasted for only a few months
In the second version there are reports of the parvenu misdeeds of the Mongols in Jerusalem and Hebron without any specific mentioning of the Christians.
the Mamlūk writers report that Mūlāy returned at the end of Jumādā II.

notes.en: Mulay's return is dated 29 Rabi' II 699 by Rashid al-Din and end of Jumada II 699 by Mamluk writers (Amitai 1987, n. 85), i.e. early 1300. Raid, not administration.
